The purpose of this work is to analyze the development direction and pro-
spects in the ﬁeld of artiﬁcial intelligence (AI) in metal–organic frameworks
(MOFs) and to provide reference information for related research and industry
personnel. The scientiﬁc papers on AI in MOFs published in Web of Science
database from 2013 to mid-2024 were collected. Bibliometric methods and
knowledge mapping visualization software were used to analyze the papers.
Both quantitative statistics and qualitative comparative analysis of global
scientiﬁc papers were done in terms of annual paper trends, papers by major
countries, authors, institutions, journals and research topics, respectively.
The results showed that the number of published papers has increased in
recent years. The top three productive countries are China, the USA and
Germany, respectively. The top three productive institutions are Guangzhou
University, Northwestern University and Chinese Academy of Sciences,
respectively. Reference co-citation analysis classiﬁes references into four
clusters, and keyword co-occurrence analysis divides keywords into six clus-
ters. Bibliometric and network analyses were utilized to examine the distri-
bution of research outcomes, enabling scholars to discern the prevailing trends
and focal points within the domain of AI-MOFs.
INTRODUCTION
Porous materials are distinguished by their net-
work structure made up of interconnected or closed
pores. According to the International Union of Pure
and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) criteria, porous
materials are categorized into three distinct groups
based on the dimensions of their pores: micropores
(<2 nm),
mesopores
(2–50 nm)
and
macropores
(>50 nm).1 The swift advancement of materials
chemistry has led to metal–organic frameworks
(MOFs) emerging as a key area of research within
the disciplines of chemistry and materials science
because of their porous nature and ongoing design
and development efforts.2–5 MOFs are a class of
compounds consisting of inorganic metal ions or
clusters coordinated with organic ligands through
self-assembly. The inaugural MOFs were synthe-
sized and designated by the research group in
1995.6 Compared to conventional porous materials,
MOFs exhibit superior thermal stability (approxi-
mately
500C),
lower
density
(approximately
200 mg/cm3), larger robust open framework struc-
ture, more speciﬁc surface area (> 8000 m2/g) and
increased porosity, among other advantageous prop-
erties. These characteristics have led to the wide-
spread utilization of MOFs in various applications
such as gas adsorption and storage, separation
processes, ion batteries, catalysis, drug delivery
systems, sensors and other ﬁelds, indicating promis-
ing prospects for their practical use.5

Due to the inherent structural adaptability of
MOFs, they have garnered signiﬁcant interest and
engagement from numerous researchers. The syn-
thesis of > 90,000 MOFs has been achieved through
experimental methods, with most of these struc-
tures cataloged in the Cambridge Structural Data-
base (CSD).7,8 Due to the swift advancement of
simulation technology and high-performance com-
puting, computers are now capable of efﬁciently
generating numerous hypothetical metal–organic
frameworks (hMOFs) by employing a variety of
secondary components (metal clusters and organic
linkers) and assembly methods. This methodology is
a valuable supplement to experimental techniques,
ultimately decreasing the time and expenses typi-
cally required for traditional material discovery, a
process often likened to locating a needle in a
haystack.9
High-throughput
computing
(HTC)
serves as a systematic theoretical methodology for
the comprehensive analysis of materials’ structural,
compositional and property-related aspects. It facil-
itates extensive theoretical forecasting by leverag-
ing
parallelized
automation
of
high-throughput
algorithms, deployed on advanced computing infras-
tructures and software frameworks.5 A thorough
assessment of the performance of MOFs across
different scenarios necessitates a detailed examina-
tion utilizing big data technology. As a result,
employing machine learning (ML) to predict the
behavior of MOFs and to explore new materials for
examining the correlation between their structure
and properties has become a signiﬁcant ﬁeld of
study, marking a notable convergence of materials
science with computational science.
Artiﬁcial intelligence (AI), a branch of computer
science, aims to develop machines that can perform
tasks typically requiring human intelligence, such
as perception, decision-making and problem-solv-
ing. Machine learning (ML), a signiﬁcant subﬁeld of
AI, relies on computational algorithms to create
models that can undertake various tasks like pre-
diction, dimensionality reduction and clustering
from the data they are trained on. ML improves
its analytical abilities through algorithmic applica-
tions and has found extensive applications in var-
ious domains, including image processing, medical
assessments,
cybersecurity
and
predictive
modeling.9,10
The utilization of machine learning algorithms for
aiding in the design of MOFs has demonstrated
signiﬁcant effectiveness in extracting relationships
between a material’s structure and its activity or
efﬁcacy and facilitating the expedited identiﬁcation
of novel high-performance materials. This has expe-
dited the shift from a reliance on random experi-
mentation to a more precise approach in the
development of MOFs.11–16
The future advancement of metal–organic frame-
works is anticipated to rely heavily on data and
artiﬁcial intelligence. Machine learning (ML) has
emerged
as
a
leading
tool
in
data-driven
methodologies, positioning itself at the forefront of
research in materials science.17–19 Machine learn-
ing offers a potent mechanism for expediting the
exploration, creation and utilization of MOFs and
has the potential to serve as a basis for fabricating
innovative MOFs with intricate characteristics.
Given its notable capacity to enhance productivity,
streamline the material development timeline and
lower the expenses associated with novel material
creation, the integration of machine learning in
MOF research is poised to emerge as a promising
avenue for future investigation.
Bibliometric analysis is a method of quantita-
tively evaluating scientiﬁc research to uncover
historical
trends,
current
research
status
and
emerging
research
directions
within
a
speciﬁc
ﬁeld.20 This approach yields reproducible and quan-
tiﬁable data that can inform policy decisions. Fur-
thermore,
bibliometric
analysis
can
offer
a
comprehensive
understanding
of
a
knowledge
domain,
pinpoint
research
gaps
and
highlight
methodologies employed by authors to address
research objectives.20,21 Utilizing bibliometric anal-
ysis, this study offers a comprehensive examination
of the utilization of artiﬁcial intelligence (AI) in
MOFs from 2013 to 2024. The results provide
insights into current trends, topics and bibliometric
characteristics within this area of research, offering
valuable information and guiding future research
directions in this rapidly evolving ﬁeld.

Bibliometric Data Analysis
VOS viewer (www.vosviewer.com) version 1.6.20
was used to construct and visualize bibliometric
networks in the current study. Bibliometric tech-
niques, such as co-authorship analysis and co-
occurrence analysis, are commonly utilized to dis-
cern
predominant themes,
explore
focal
points
within the literature and visually represent the
annual output of publications, journals, authors,
countries, institutions, collaboration networks, key-
words and references. In VOSviewer visualization
maps, nodes are depicted as circles with correspond-
ing labels, with larger circles denoting higher
frequencies in co-occurrence analysis. The color of
each circle signiﬁes its cluster afﬁliation, while the
thickness and length of links between nodes convey
the strength of their connections.
RESULTS
Annual Distributions of Publications
Our analysis focused on the annual growth of the
study, speciﬁcally examining the publication year of
articles. Figure 2 illustrates the distribution of
articles by year from 2013 to 2024, along with a
model-ﬁtting curve depicting the global trends in
publication growth. These ﬁndings suggest that
there is a growing interest among researchers in the
ﬁeld of AI in MOFs. The search of electronic
databases yielded 912 records. Following the review
of titles and abstracts, 189 entries were removed.
Ultimately, 723 papers were selected for the deﬁni-
tive bibliometric analysis.

across 237 international peer-reviewed journals.

An examination of co-authorship patterns among

The ﬁeld of artiﬁcial intelligence has experienced
signiﬁcant growth, with over 700 publications since
2013. If this growth trend persists, it is anticipated
that
the
number
of
publications
in
AI
-MOF
research will triple in the next 5 years. Machine
learning, as an integral branch of AI, holds great
potential for propelling the evolution of MOF mate-
rials by analyzing their complex structures and
attributes. The application of machine learning
within the realm of MOF research is experiencing
a signiﬁcant upswing, with these algorithms being
utilized to predict and reﬁne both the architecture
and functionality of MOFs. This trend underscores
the growing reliance on ML for advancing the
development and optimization of these materials.
Creating an exhaustive database that includes a
wide range of data on MOF structures and charac-
teristics is essential, covering details like crystalline
forms, pore sizes, porosity levels, adsorptive capac-
ities and additional pertinent attributes. By lever-
aging machine learning algorithms, the objective of
effectively and expeditiously identifying high-per-
forming MOF materials can be realized, thereby
diminishing the expenses and duration required for
experimental exploration through iterative trial-
and-error in the laboratory.
ML can promote the development of MOF mate-
rials by analyzing their complex structures and
properties. The main application directions in the
MOF ﬁeld are: (1) Classiﬁcation: Learning the
relationship between the features and labels of
sample data to classify new data. Smit and col-
leagues employed a data-driven strategy to develop
MOFs capable of high CO2 adsorption in humid ﬂue
gas, successfully identifying > 300,000 MOFs with
potent
CO2
binding
afﬁnities.30
Anderson
and
Go´mez-Gualdro´n introduced an innovative compu-
tational framework featuring a multilayer percep-
tron (MLP) model, which efﬁciently identiﬁes MOFs
with superior separation capabilities for mixed
gases at reduced computational expense.31 (2) Pre-
diction: ML in MOFs is primarily rooted in its
capacity to establish correlations between struc-
tural features and speciﬁc properties as well as to
discern the most effective descriptors for their
precise prediction. In 2023, Sheng et al.32 used
density functional theory (DFT) and molecular
dynamics
(MD)

a

predict CO2 adsorption and CO2/N2 selectivity,

preparation in carbon capture applications. Abdi

Identifying optimal synthesis pathways within the
expansive material space to minimize experimental
trials and costs has become a critical focus, with
global optimization algorithms such as Bayesian
Optimization (BO) and Genetic Algorithms (GA)
emerging as valuable aids in chemical synthesis. In
2019, Moosavi et al.34 ﬁrst used the GA algorithm to
optimize the experimental synthesis conditions of
MOFs. Based on the experimental trajectory of
failed HKUST-1 synthesis, they found the optimal
conditions for synthesizing HKUST-1 with a high
speciﬁc surface area. Following this, in 2022, Zhang
et al.35 employed a suite of ML models, including
linear regression, adaboost regression, gradient
boosting decision tree (GBDT) regression and ran-
dom forest regression, to analyze particle size
variations in Eu-MOFs and determine the most
effective synthesis conditions.

and regulation of their structure and performance.

fosters the utilization of MOFs in processes such as

CONCLUSION
Artiﬁcial intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing key
aspects of materials science, garnering substantial
interest from both academic and industrial experts.
This bibliometric analysis provides an in-depth
examination of the global trends and research
landscape
of
AI
in
metal–organic
frameworks
(MOFs) from 2013 to 2024. By identifying the most
productive countries, institutions, authors and the
state of research technologies relevant to MOFs,
this study outlines the current advancements and
emerging trends within the ﬁeld.
The convergence of challenges and opportunities
in AI-MOF research presents a dynamic and fertile
ground for innovation. Enhancing data quality and
model interpretability, alongside algorithmic inno-
vation and interdisciplinary collaboration, is essen-
tial for driving new advancements in materials
science. The coming years are anticipated to witness
a signiﬁcant increase in AI-driven breakthroughs,
accelerating the development of novel materials
with unparalleled properties and functionalities.
The integration of machine learning (ML) and
MOFs is expected to signiﬁcantly bolster the rapid
progress of both computer science and materials
science, fostering a symbiotic relationship that
enhances the advancement of both disciplines.
The bibliometric analysis conducted in this study
reveals a vibrant research ﬁeld on the cusp of
signiﬁcant innovation. As the research community
continues to improve data quality, model inter-
pretability and algorithmic innovation, while also
fostering interdisciplinary partnerships, we stand
on the brink of a new era of advancements in
